name: International Protection (Refugee Status / Subsidiary Protection)

qualifying_event.description: The Directorate of Immigration decides applications for international protection. Applicants must be physically present in Iceland; applications from abroad are not processed. Submitted in person (a verbal statement suffices) at Keflavik Airport police, the Reykjavik reception centre, or the nearest police station.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: In-person application; interview with the Directorate of Immigration; supporting documents where available.

requirements.blocker_text: The Directorate of Immigration assesses eligibility for refugee status or the lesser subsidiary protection status.
Must be physically present in Iceland to apply; applications sent from abroad are not processed.

evidence_required.document: Grounds for protection presented at interview, with supporting documents where available

outcome.duration_length: Refugee status: 3-year permit; Subsidiary protection: 2-year permit, renewable before expiration

sources.title: Island.is -- International Protection, Rights and Application Procedure: Directorate of Immigration process, physical-presence requirement, in-person application at Keflavik Airport/Reykjavik reception centre/police stations

Island.is -- Residence Permits on Grounds of International Protection: refugee status 3-year permit, unrestricted work rights, family reunification rules (before/after protection granted, 4-year prior work/study for post-grant spouses/children)

Island.is -- Residence Permit on Grounds of Subsidiary Protection: 2-year permit, unrestricted work rights, labour/housing/language pathway to family reunification after 1 year (8+ months employment, ISK 259,951/month income, 80 hours Icelandic instruction, secured lease)

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Iceland). Strong tier-1 sourcing throughout, unusual for this category in this dataset. Family reunification for international protection holders is genuinely two-tiered and disclosed precisely rather than simplified: family members who existed BEFORE protection was granted (spouse/cohabiting partner from before, children under 18 born before, parents 67+) qualify under one track; family formed AFTER protection was granted requires either 4 years of prior work/study in Iceland, OR (for subsidiary protection specifically) a 1-year labour/housing/language pathway with specific ISK income and Icelandic-instruction-hours conditions -- not fully modeled as separate requirement groups here to avoid excessive complexity, but flagged in detail since this materially affects real applicants. study_rights modeled 'restricted' as a conservative default since neither source explicitly confirmed study rights during status (only work rights were explicit).
